original.title: Dispatch Loom
original.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
original.summary: Internal dispatch reconciliation tool for comparing an overnight spreadsheet with a daily export and surfacing understandable exceptions. Personally designed and built by Ada Rowan, who wrote the Python parser and SQL checks; coworkers also changed their checking habits, so the measured improvement was a team result. Operators kept empty rows visible because a blank reference could require a phone call, and late-arriving source files prompted a visible warning. The supervisor made the final dispatch decision.

decisions.reason: The source describes Dispatch Loom as an operational reconciliation tool, personally designed and built by Ada, with the stated parser, checks, workflow, warning, empty-row handling, team improvement context, and supervisor decision authority.
Ada explicitly says she personally designed and built Dispatch Loom.
Ada says she designed and built Dispatch Loom using Python and separately says she wrote its Python parser herself.
Ada says she designed and built Dispatch Loom using SQL and separately says she wrote its SQL checks herself.
Ada explicitly says she wrote the Python parser and SQL checks herself.
The source gives the reduction from 5 to 2 hours per week, measured over six weekly runs, and identifies it as a team result.
Ada identifies the parser and checks as her contribution to the team result.
The source says operators compared the overnight spreadsheet against the daily export.
The source says the dispatch desk dealt with mismatched references rather than delivery route optimization.
Ada explicitly says she gathered Dispatch Loom requirements from warehouse supervisors.
Ada explicitly says she explained validation failures to warehouse supervisors.
Ada says she used Git for version control.
Ada says PostgreSQL was the production database.
The source says they kept empty rows visible because a blank reference might require a phone call.
The source says the source file could arrive late and operators preferred a visible warning.
The source says the handbook described where a coworker should look before raising an exception.
The source says the supervisor made the final dispatch decision.
The source explicitly states that delivery speed was not measured.
The source explicitly says no machine-learning classifier was involved in the rules.
Ada explicitly says she did not own the warehouse staffing budget.
Ada explicitly says she did not own procurement.
Ada explicitly says she did not own the scheduling system.
The source says delivery speed was not measured and that the six-run measurement describes reconciliation work only.
Ada says coworkers also changed their checking habits and she cannot attribute all the improvement to herself.
The source says the parser and SQL checks worked together as one piece of work, and that Git changes and PostgreSQL production data were not separate products.
